body: One remaining editorial/IA finding after the source-level fixes: the site now has seven executable task pages, but the splash page directly routes only to align, model, and source inspection. Its “What the source library provides” bullets also omit whole existing areas that matter to the owner’s “big library” question: proposition/AMR interop, autonomous proposal-critic-resolution acquisition, document/coreference compilation, and feature/embedding generation. Please add a compact linked task map from the homepage to represent recall, summarize, score interview, save/verify, and embeddings, and broaden the capability summary to cover those existing module families without implying publication or raw-text completeness. The module map is accurate but should be the detail behind the front-door answer, not the only place those capabilities are discoverable. Non-blocking until the immutable candidate, but material to the sixty-second comprehension gate.
